final.title: Solid-State Battery Market Outlook: Size, Growth, Key Players, and Challenges
final.summary: The global solid-state battery market is poised for rapid growth, driven primarily by automotive applications. According to Helix Research, the market reached $1.9 billion in revenue in 2025 and is projected to grow to $8.4 billion by 2030, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 34.6%. Aster Analytics offers a slightly higher estimate of $2.6 billion for 2025 (including pilot-line sample sales) and $7.9 billion by 2030. Automotive applications account for 62% of demand, followed by consumer electronics at 21% and grid storage at 9%. Asia-Pacific leads with 48% of installed manufacturing capacity, followed by Europe at 31% and North America at 17%. The first mass-market electric vehicles with solid-state packs are expected to ship in late 2027.

findings.claim: The global solid-state battery market reached $1.9 billion in revenue in 2025 and is projected to grow to $8.4 billion by 2030, a compound annual growth rate of 34.6%, according to Helix Research.
Aster Analytics estimates the solid-state battery market at $2.6 billion in 2025 (including pilot-line sample sales) and expects it to reach $7.9 billion by 2030.

Automotive applications account for 62% of solid-state battery demand, followed by consumer electronics at 21% and grid storage at 9%. Analysts expect the first mass-market electric vehicles with solid-state packs to ship in late 2027.

Quantor Cells is the market leader with an estimated 27% share of 2025 solid-state battery revenue, using a sulfide electrolyte. Its two main rivals are Lumisolid (oxide electrolyte) and Hesper Energy (polymer electrolyte).
Quantor Cells opened a 12 GWh solid-state battery plant in Leipzig, Germany, in March 2026, and has a supply agreement with Ardent Motors for its 2027 sedan.
Asia-Pacific holds 48% of installed solid-state battery manufacturing capacity, Europe 31%, and North America 17%.

Key challenges include lithium dendrite growth through the electrolyte under fast charging, high costs (solid-state cells cost about $210 per kWh in 2025 compared with $115 per kWh for lithium-ion packs), and low manufacturing yields (average 71% in 2025 versus more than 95% for mature lithium-ion lines).
Lower prices for conventional lithium-ion packs, which fell to $115 per kWh in 2025 (down 14% from the prior year), make it harder for solid-state batteries to compete on cost.

final.title: RISC-V Edge AI Chip Market Overview
final.summary: The RISC-V edge AI chip market reached $3.1 billion in 2025, with 2.4 billion RISC-V cores shipped in edge devices. The market is projected to grow to $9.7 billion by 2029, driven primarily by rising licensing costs for proprietary CPU cores and growing demand for AI at the edge. Industrial IoT is the largest application segment at 37% of revenue, followed by smart cameras (24%) and wearables (15%). Veltrix Semiconductors leads with 41% of design wins, followed by Corvana (22%, focused on automotive-grade chips) and Openfab Systems (13%). The EU is also investing EUR 270 million in open instruction-set chip design between 2026 and 2028.

findings.claim: The RISC-V edge AI chip market reached $3.1 billion in 2025, with 2.4 billion RISC-V cores shipped in edge devices, and is forecast to reach $9.7 billion by 2029.
Industrial IoT is the largest market segment at 37% of revenue, followed by smart cameras at 24% and wearables at 15%.

final.title: State of the Vertical Farming Market: Size, Key Players, and Economics
final.summary: The vertical farming market was valued at $6.3 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $11.8 billion by 2030. The industry experienced a significant shake-out in 2024 when two large operators went bankrupt, primarily due to unsustainable energy costs. Energy now accounts for 38% of a typical vertical farm's operating expenses. Leafy greens dominate production, representing 71% of output. Key surviving companies include Canopy Grid (which raised $140 million in Series C funding for a 9-hectare facility near Rotterdam, the largest in Europe) and Tierra Vertical (operating 14 smaller farms across Spain and Portugal). The economics remain challenging: vertical farm lettuce costs approximately $3.90 per kg to produce compared to $1.60 per kg for field-grown lettuce. The two biggest levers to close this cost gap are lower electricity prices and higher automation. Horticultural LED technology has improved, reaching an efficacy of 3.4 micromoles per joule in 2025, but energy-intensive operations continue to pressure profitability.

Technical barriers include stack degradation and low utilization rates when running on intermittent renewable energy sources.

final.title: Plant-Based Meat Market: Sales, Growth, Leading Brands, and Challenges
final.summary: The plant-based meat market experienced a slowdown in 2025 after three years of growth. Global sales reached $6.9 billion in 2025, down 4% from 2024. Retail volumes fell 7% in the United States but grew 9% in Asia, indicating regional divergence. The market is led by Verdant Foods with 22% global market share, followed by Proteus at 15%. Key challenges include a significant price gap—plant-based burgers cost 43% more per kg than beef burgers—and consumer dissatisfaction with taste and texture, which are the top reasons shoppers do not repurchase. The industry is responding by exploring precision-fermentation proteins to reduce ingredient costs by approximately 30% compared to traditional pea protein sources.

findings.claim: Global plant-based meat sales were $6.9 billion in 2025, down 4% from 2024 after three years of growth.
Retail volumes fell 7% in the United States but grew 9% in Asia, showing regional divergence in market performance.

final.title: eVTOL Air Taxi Market Outlook: Forecast, Manufacturers, and Barriers
final.summary: The eVTOL air taxi market remains pre-commercial as of late 2025, with no services in operation. Market forecasts vary significantly: Skyline Research projects the passenger-focused market at $1.2 billion in 2028 growing to $9.8 billion by 2033, while MarketPulse estimates $3.5 billion in 2028 by including cargo drones and pilot training. The leading manufacturer is AeroVolt with 2,100 aircraft orders and expected type certification in early 2027, followed by Skylane with 1,350 orders. Total order books across all manufacturers stand at 7,400 aircraft. Key barriers include limited battery range (~100 km), noise restrictions in urban areas, insufficient vertiport infrastructure, and the ongoing regulatory certification process.
